title: CEC Code Assistant protocol pack
note: Decision support for trained staff of the Cardiac Emergency Centre, SGHL. Written in our own words from the sources listed; the doctor stays responsible.

AHA25-ALS.name: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and ECC, Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, with the 2025 ACLS algorithms (Cardiac Arrest, Bradycardia With a Pulse, Tachyarrhythmia With a Pulse, Electrical Cardioversion)

AHA25-SPEC.name: 2025 AHA Guidelines, Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation (pregnancy 19.3, pulmonary embolism 20.2, hyperkalaemia 15)

AHA25-PCAC.name: 2025 AHA Guidelines, Part 11: Post-Cardiac Arrest Care

ERC25-ALS.name: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025: Adult Advanced Life Support

RCUK25.name: Resuscitation Council UK Guidelines 2025 (UK adaptation of ERC 2025): Adult ALS, Adult ALS algorithm, Adult bradyarrhythmia algorithm (2025), Adult tachyarrhythmia algorithm (version 3, March 2026)
RCUK25.pub: resus.org.uk, published 27-10-2025; tachyarrhythmia algorithm updated March 2026

RCUK25-SPEC.name: Resuscitation Council UK 2025 Special circumstances guidelines (from ERC Guidelines 2025 Special Circumstances, Resuscitation 2025;215 Suppl 1:110753)

ESC19-SVT.name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the management of patients with supraventricular tachycardia (still the current ESC SVT guideline in November 2026)

ESC22-VA.name: 2022 ESC Guidelines for the management of patients with ventricular arrhythmias and the prevention of sudden cardiac death

ESC24-AF.name: 2024 ESC Guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation

ESC21-PACE.name: 2021 ESC Guidelines on cardiac pacing and cardiac resynchronization therapy

ESC23-ACS.name: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes (the next ESC ACS guideline is planned for 2027)

ACCAHA25-ACS.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes
ACCAHA25-ACS.pub: Circulation 2025;151:e771-e862 and J Am Coll Cardiol 2025;85:2135-2237 (published 27-02-2025)

UDMI5.name: Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2026), ESC/ACC/AHA/WHF. Changes the classification of MI (primary, secondary, procedure-related); it does not change the emergency steps in this pack

ESC26-HF.name: 2026 ESC Guidelines for the management of heart failure (replaces the 2021 guideline and the 2023 focused update; 'decompensated HF' replaces 'acute HF'; HFrEF now means LVEF below 50%)

ESC21-HF.name: 2021 ESC Guidelines for acute and chronic heart failure (replaced by ESC 2026; used here ONLY for the infusion dose ranges of inotropes and vasopressors, which the 2026 text was not checked for)

ESC24-HTN.name: 2024 ESC Guidelines for the management of elevated blood pressure and hypertension

ESC19-HTNEM.name: ESC Council on Hypertension position document on the management of hypertensive emergencies (van den Born et al.), the drug and target table used by the ESC 2024 guideline

AHAACC25-HBP.name: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (section 6.2: hypertensive emergencies)

ESC25-PREG.name: 2025 ESC Guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and pregnancy (29-08-2025)

ACOG767.name: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 767: Emergent therapy for acute-onset, severe hypertension during pregnancy and the postpartum period (IV labetalol and hydralazine dose steps)

LABEL.name: Drug reference (second check of doses): the manufacturers' US prescribing information as summarised by Drugs.com professional dosing pages, read 26-11-2026. (The BNF website could not be opened from here; Dr. Hammad may check the BNF.)

MCMASTER.name: McMaster Textbook of Internal Medicine, table 'Fibrinolysis in patients with STEMI' (doses as in the ESC STEMI tables; second check of the heparin and enoxaparin doses with fibrinolysis)

epi_arrest.route: IV (IO if IV is not possible)
epi_arrest.how: 1 mg of the 1 mg/10 mL (0.1 mg/mL) syringe as a bolus, then flush 20 mL saline and raise the arm.
epi_arrest.repeat: Every 3 to 5 minutes while the arrest continues (about every second 2-minute cycle).
epi_arrest.timing: Non-shockable rhythm (asystole, PEA): give as soon as possible. Shockable rhythm (VF, pulseless VT): give after the first shocks have failed (AHA algorithm: after the 2nd shock).
epi_arrest.max: No maximum during the arrest. High doses are not recommended.
epi_arrest.watch: After ROSC: tachycardia, high BP, new arrhythmia.

preg.text: Same dose in pregnancy. Do not hold back any resuscitation drug because of the baby.

src: AHA25-ALS|Section 10 (Rec 2-4, 6) and Adult Cardiac Arrest Algorithm, Drug therapy
epi_arrest.check: LABEL: 1 mg IV or IO every 3 to 5 minutes (agrees).
epi_arrest.diff: ERC / RCUK 2025: in a shockable rhythm the first epinephrine is given after the 3rd shock (AHA 2025: after the 2nd shock). The app prompts after the 2nd shock (AHA) and notes the ERC timing.
epi_arrest.name: Epinephrine (adrenaline) in cardiac arrest

amio_arrest.how: 300 mg as an IV / IO bolus (as your pharmacy supplies it), then flush well. 2nd dose 150 mg.
amio_arrest.watch: After ROSC: low BP, slow heart rate.
amio_arrest.contra: None in VF / pulseless VT arrest. Do not use for torsades de pointes (use magnesium).

lqt: Torsades (long QT): use magnesium; amiodarone lengthens the QT.

preg.text: Give it in arrest if needed (life first). Outside arrest it is avoided in pregnancy except for life-threatening arrhythmias.

src: AHA25-ALS|Section 11 Rec 1 and Adult Cardiac Arrest Algorithm (amiodarone 300 mg, then 150 mg)
amio_arrest.check: LABEL: amiodarone label gives 150 mg loading for unstable VT/recurrent VF with pulse; the arrest dose (300 mg, 150 mg) is from the resuscitation guidelines.
amio_arrest.diff: AHA 2025 gives amiodarone OR lidocaine equal standing (class 2b).
amio_arrest.name: Amiodarone in cardiac arrest (VF / pulseless VT)

lido_arrest.how: Plain lidocaine 2% (20 mg/mL) without adrenaline. 70 kg: 70-105 mg first.
lido_arrest.watch: After ROSC: confusion, fits, slow rhythm.
lido_arrest.contra: Lidocaine allergy; heart block without pacing (after ROSC).

preg.text: May be used in pregnancy (it is the usual local anaesthetic).

src: AHA25-ALS|Adult Cardiac Arrest Algorithm (lidocaine 1-1.5 mg/kg, then 0.5-0.75 mg/kg)
lido_arrest.check: LABEL (AHA-based dosing): 1-1.5 mg/kg, then 0.5-0.75 mg/kg every 5-10 min, total 3 mg/kg (agrees).
lido_arrest.name: Lidocaine in cardiac arrest (if amiodarone is not available)

calcium_cl.route: IV, through a large vein (it burns if it leaks)
calcium_cl.how: In cardiac arrest: rapid IV bolus. With a pulse: over 5 minutes. Flush before and after, and do not give it in the same line as sodium bicarbonate (it precipitates).
calcium_cl.max: May repeat once if the ECG still shows hyperkalaemia.
calcium_cl.watch: Leak into the tissues (necrosis); slow heart rate.
calcium_cl.contra: Digoxin toxicity (use only on expert advice).

preg.text: Give it: in a pregnant woman who arrests while on IV magnesium sulfate, calcium is reasonable.

src: RCUK25-SPEC|Hyperkalaemia: 10 mL 10% calcium chloride IV (with 50 mmol sodium bicarbonate in hyperkalaemic arrest)
AHA25-SPEC|§15: IV calcium for hyperkalaemic arrest, class 2b
calcium_cl.check: LABEL (calcium chloride): 200-1000 mg (2-10 mL of 10%) slow IV for low calcium; the hyperkalaemia dose is from RCUK 2025. Second check of the hyperkalaemia dose: pending (BNF).
calcium_cl.diff: AHA 2025 says the benefit of calcium in hyperkalaemic arrest is not well established (2b); RCUK 2025 recommends it.
calcium_cl.name: Calcium chloride 10% (hyperkalaemia, low calcium, magnesium overdose, calcium-channel blocker overdose)

calcium_gluc.how: Over 10 minutes with a pulse; as a bolus in cardiac arrest.
calcium_gluc.watch: Slow heart rate; leak into tissues.

preg.text: Used in pregnancy (it is the antidote for magnesium toxicity: 30 mL 10% IV).

src: RCUK25-SPEC|Hyperkalaemia: if calcium chloride is not available, 30 mL 10% calcium gluconate over 10 min
calcium_gluc.check: Second source: ESC 2025 pregnancy guideline (30 mL 10% calcium gluconate IV for magnesium toxicity).
calcium_gluc.name: Calcium gluconate 10% (when calcium chloride is not available)

bicarb.how: Rapid IV, through a separate line from calcium, or flush well between them.
bicarb.watch: High sodium, low calcium, tissue damage if it leaks.
bicarb.contra: Not for routine use in cardiac arrest.
src: RCUK25-SPEC|Hyperkalaemic cardiac arrest: 50 mmol sodium bicarbonate IV
AHA25-ALS|Section 11 Rec 5: routine bicarbonate not recommended
AHA25-SPEC|§15: bicarbonate in hyperkalaemic arrest, class 2b
bicarb.name: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% (hyperkalaemic cardiac arrest only)

doses: Soluble (regular) insulin 10 units + glucose 25 g IV
insulin_glu.how: Glucose 25 g = 50 mL of 50% or 125 mL of 20%, with 10 units soluble insulin (AHA: insulin over 15-30 minutes). Then check glucose often; if the glucose before treatment was below 7 mmol/L (126 mg/dL), run 10% glucose 50 mL/h for 5 hours (RCUK).
insulin_glu.watch: Low blood sugar for up to 6 hours.
src: RCUK25-SPEC|Hyperkalaemia: 10 units soluble insulin and 25 g glucose IV
AHA25-SPEC|§15 Table 3: 10 units regular insulin with 50 g glucose
insulin_glu.check: Two guidelines agree on 10 units of insulin.
insulin_glu.diff: Glucose: RCUK 2025 gives 25 g; AHA 2025 gives 50 g (with the same 10 units). The app shows 25 g with the glucose checks (RCUK) and notes the AHA amount.
insulin_glu.name: Insulin with glucose (moves potassium into cells)

alteplase_pe.how: Senior decision. Give when PE is the likely cause (sudden breathlessness before collapse, risk factors, dilated RV on echo). Continue CPR for 60 to 90 minutes after giving it.
alteplase_pe.contra: Weigh against active bleeding, recent surgery, stroke or head injury.

preg.text: Life-threatening PE in pregnancy: fibrinolysis can be given (bleeding risk, including from the placenta).
src: ESC25-PREG|§12.2 (rtPA does not cross the placenta; bleeding risk)
AHA25-SPEC|§20.2 Rec 1 and 3: fibrinolysis reasonable in confirmed PE arrest (2a), may be considered in suspected PE (2b)
RCUK25-SPEC|Use fibrinolytic drugs when PE is the suspected cause of arrest
alteplase_pe.check: DOSE NOT FIXED BY THE 2025 GUIDELINES: 50 mg bolus is the regimen most used (British Thoracic Society 2003; case reports). Dr. Hammad to confirm before use.
alteplase_pe.name: Alteplase for cardiac arrest from pulmonary embolism

adenosine.route: IV, fast push into a large arm vein (antecubital)
adenosine.how: Push in 1-2 seconds through a 3-way tap and flush at once with 20 mL saline; raise the arm. Run a rhythm strip while giving. Warn the patient: a few seconds of chest tightness and a feeling of doom.
adenosine.max: 12 mg (AHA, label) or 18 mg (RCUK) as a single dose.
adenosine.watch: A pause or brief asystole, flushing, breathlessness, chest discomfort, rarely AF. Have the defibrillator ready.
adenosine.contra: Asthma or COPD with bronchospasm; pre-excited AF (irregular wide fast); 2nd or 3rd degree AV block or sick sinus without a pacemaker.
adenosine.cautions: Through a central line or after a heart transplant a much smaller first dose works (AHA 2025: 1 mg may be enough). Dipyridamole and carbamazepine strengthen its effect; theophylline and caffeine weaken it.

pxaf: Not for irregular or polymorphic wide tachycardia (pre-excited AF).
wpw: Known WPW: adenosine can start AF with fast conduction; have the defibrillator ready.

preg.text: Safe in pregnancy: first drug after vagal manoeuvres (6-18 mg).

src: AHA25-ALS|Section 17 Rec 2 and Tachyarrhythmia algorithm, Doses/Details (6 mg, then 12 mg)
ESC19-SVT|Acute therapy of narrow QRS tachycardia (adenosine 6-18 mg)
adenosine.check: LABEL: 6 mg rapid bolus; if no effect in 1-2 min 12 mg, which may be repeated once (agrees).
adenosine.diff: RCUK 2025 and ESC 2019 allow 18 mg as the third dose; AHA 2025 stops at 12 mg (the label repeats 12 mg).
adenosine.name: Adenosine

verapamil.how: Slowly over at least 2 minutes (3 minutes in older patients), with ECG and BP monitoring.
verapamil.watch: Low BP, slow heart rate, heart block.
verapamil.contra: Low BP or shock; heart failure with low EF; wide-complex tachycardia (may be VT); pre-excited AF / WPW; IV beta-blocker given recently; 2nd/3rd degree block.

hfref: Weakens the heart muscle: avoid in heart failure with low EF or acute heart failure.
pxaf: Speeds conduction down the accessory pathway: can cause VF.
wpw: Known pre-excitation: avoid AV-node blockers if AF / flutter is possible.

preg.text: Can be used in pregnancy (2.5-10 mg over 5 min).

src: AHA25-ALS|Section 17 Rec 5 (stable regular narrow-complex), Section 15 Rec 5 and 18.2 Rec 3-4 (harm in wide-complex, pre-excited AF, decompensated HFrEF)
RCUK25|Adult tachyarrhythmia algorithm (verapamil or beta-blocker after adenosine)
verapamil.check: LABEL: 5-10 mg (0.075-0.15 mg/kg) over at least 2 min; 10 mg after 30 min if needed (agrees).
verapamil.name: Verapamil IV

diltiazem.how: Each bolus over 2 minutes; infusion for rate control after the bolus.
diltiazem.contra: As verapamil: low BP, heart failure with low EF, wide-complex tachycardia, pre-excitation.

hfref: Avoid in heart failure with low EF or acute heart failure.
pxaf: Can cause VF in pre-excited AF.

preg.text: Little data in pregnancy; verapamil or metoprolol are preferred.

src: AHA25-ALS|Section 17 Rec 5 and 18.2 Rec 1 (non-dihydropyridine calcium blockers)
diltiazem.check: LABEL: 0.25 mg/kg over 2 min; 0.35 mg/kg after 15 min; infusion 10 mg/h, 5 mg/h steps to 15 mg/h, up to 24 h (agrees).
diltiazem.name: Diltiazem IV

metoprolol_iv.how: Over 2 minutes; repeat every 5 minutes if needed.
metoprolol_iv.watch: Low BP, slow rate, wheeze, worsening heart failure.
metoprolol_iv.contra: Shock or low BP; acute decompensated heart failure; asthma with wheeze; 2nd/3rd degree block; pre-excited AF.

asthma: Beta-1 selective, but can still cause wheeze; avoid in active bronchospasm.
hfref: Low EF: only if not in acute heart failure and BP is good; start with 2.5 mg.
pxaf: AV-node blocker: avoid in pre-excited AF.

preg.text: Beta-1 selective blocker of choice in pregnancy (2.5-15 mg IV). Atenolol is the only contraindicated beta-blocker.

src: ESC19-SVT|Metoprolol 2.5-15 mg IV in 2.5 mg boluses
AHA25-ALS|Section 18.2 Rec 1 (IV beta-blockers for AF/flutter rate control)
metoprolol_iv.check: LABEL (acute MI regimen): 5 mg IV every 2 min to 15 mg; the label has no SVT regimen. Doses agree on the 15 mg total.
metoprolol_iv.name: Metoprolol IV

esmolol.how: Rate control: load, then 50 micrograms/kg/min, raised every 4 minutes (each step may have another load). Aortic dissection / severe BP: up to 250-300 micrograms/kg/min.
esmolol.max: 200 micrograms/kg/min for heart rate; 300 for blood pressure.
esmolol.watch: Low BP (wears off in 10-20 minutes after stopping).
esmolol.contra: As other beta-blockers: shock, decompensated heart failure, bronchospasm, high-grade block, pre-excited AF.

asthma: Beta-1 selective; avoid in active bronchospasm.
hfref: Only if not in acute heart failure.

preg.text: Short-term use only if needed; metoprolol is better studied.

src: ESC19-HTNEM|Esmolol 0.5-1 mg/kg bolus, 50-300 micrograms/kg/min (acute aortic disease)
esmolol.check: LABEL: 500 micrograms/kg over 1 min, 50 micrograms/kg/min, steps every 4 min; up to 200 (rate) or 300 (BP) micrograms/kg/min (agrees).
esmolol.name: Esmolol IV

doses: 8 to 12 micrograms/kg (about 0.5 mg first, then 0.25 mg every 6-8 h for 2 doses)
digoxin_iv.how: Each dose over at least 5 minutes. Half the total first, then a quarter every 6-8 hours twice. Slow onset (hours).
digoxin_iv.max: Total loading as above; lower in kidney failure and in the elderly.
digoxin_iv.watch: Nausea, visual change, heart block, new arrhythmia; check potassium.
digoxin_iv.contra: Pre-excited AF / WPW; 2nd or 3rd degree block; hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy; low potassium.

pxaf: Can cause VF in pre-excited AF.
ckd: Kidney failure: lower and slower dosing; check level.

preg.text: Can be used in pregnancy for rate control.

src: ESC24-AF|Acute rate control: beta-blockers or digoxin when LVEF is 40% or less
RCUK25|Adult tachyarrhythmia algorithm: EF < 40% beta-blocker or digoxin
digoxin_iv.check: LABEL: total loading 8-12 micrograms/kg IV: half first, then a quarter every 6-8 h twice; inject over 5 min or longer (agrees).
digoxin_iv.name: Digoxin IV (rate control when the heart is weak)

doses: 150 mg over 10 minutes (AHA); RCUK: 300 mg over 10-60 minutes
1 mg/min for 6 hours (360 mg), then 0.5 mg/min for 18 hours
amio_tachy.route: IV infusion, best through a large or central vein (it irritates veins)
amio_tachy.how: Dilute in 5% glucose. Repeat 150 mg over 10 min if VT returns.
amio_tachy.max: Low BP becomes more common above 2.1 g in the first 24 hours (label).
amio_tachy.watch: Low BP, slow rate, QT lengthening; phlebitis.
amio_tachy.contra: Pre-excited AF (IV amiodarone can speed conduction: harm); torsades de pointes / long QT; 2nd/3rd degree block without pacing.

pxaf: AHA 2025 and ESC 2019: IV amiodarone is harmful in pre-excited AF.
lqt: Long QT / torsades: do not give amiodarone (RCUK: avoid).

preg.text: Not recommended in pregnancy except for refractory or life-threatening arrhythmias, with foetal monitoring.

src: AHA25-ALS|Tachyarrhythmia algorithm Doses/Details (150 mg over 10 min, repeat if VT recurs, 1 mg/min for 6 h)
RCUK25|Adult tachyarrhythmia algorithm (300 mg IV over 10-20 min after failed shocks; 300 mg over 10-60 min then 900 mg over 24 h)
amio_tachy.check: LABEL: 150 mg over 10 min, then 360 mg over 6 h (1 mg/min), then 540 mg over 18 h (0.5 mg/min); breakthrough 150 mg over 10 min (agrees with AHA).
amio_tachy.diff: RCUK 2025 uses 300 mg as the first dose (over 10-20 min after failed shocks; over 10-60 min in stable VT). AHA 2025 and the label: 150 mg over 10 min.
amio_tachy.name: Amiodarone IV (tachycardia with a pulse)

doses: 20-50 mg/min (AHA) or 10-15 mg/kg over 20 min (RCUK, max 1 g)
procainamide.how: Stop the loading when the arrhythmia stops, the BP falls, the QRS widens by more than 50%, or 17 mg/kg has been given.
procainamide.watch: Low BP, QRS and QT widening.
procainamide.contra: Long QT / torsades; heart failure; complete heart block; lupus.

ckd: Severe kidney failure: lower loading (12 mg/kg) and maintenance.

preg.text: Limited pregnancy data; use only on specialist advice.
src: ESC25-PREG|§12.4.2 (drug choice depends on the substrate)
RCUK25|Adult tachyarrhythmia algorithm v3 2026 (10-15 mg/kg over 20 min)
ESC22-VA|Tolerated monomorphic VT: IV procainamide should be considered
procainamide.check: LABEL: ACLS 20 mg/min (up to 50) to the same end points, 17 mg/kg; maintenance 1-4 mg/min (agrees). Often not available in Pakistan.
procainamide.name: Procainamide IV

lido_vt.how: Plain lidocaine (no adrenaline). Halve doses in liver failure, shock and the elderly.
lido_vt.max: 3 mg/kg in total (label: 300 mg in one hour).

preg.text: Can be used in pregnancy.

src: AHA25-ALS|Lidocaine doses (cardiac arrest algorithm); stable VT antiarrhythmics Section 15 Rec 3
lido_vt.check: LABEL: 1-1.5 mg/kg, then 0.5-0.75 mg/kg every 5-10 min, total 3 mg/kg; infusion 1-4 mg/min (agrees).
lido_vt.diff: ESC 2019 removed lidocaine from the acute wide-complex tachycardia algorithm; it stays here only as a fallback.
lido_vt.name: Lidocaine IV (stable VT, when amiodarone / procainamide are not available)

doses: 60 kg or more: 1 mg over 10 minutes; below 60 kg: 0.01 mg/kg over 10 minutes
Repeat once after 10 min if needed
ibutilide.how: Stop as soon as the rhythm converts or any VT / QT lengthening appears. ECG monitor for at least 4 hours after.
ibutilide.contra: Long QT, low potassium or magnesium, severe heart failure.

hfref: Higher risk of torsades in low EF.

preg.text: May be considered in pregnancy for stable AF (ESC 2025).
src: ESC25-PREG|§12.4.1.2 (IV ibutilide or flecainide may be considered)

ibutilide.check: LABEL: 1 mg over 10 min (60 kg or more), 0.01 mg/kg below 60 kg, repeat once after 10 min; monitor 4 h (agrees). Rarely available in Pakistan.
ibutilide.name: Ibutilide IV (pre-excited AF, AF or flutter)

flecainide_iv.how: Only with a normal heart: no old MI, no heart failure, no significant LV hypertrophy.
flecainide_iv.watch: QRS widening, low BP, conversion to flutter with 1:1 conduction.
flecainide_iv.contra: Ischaemic or structural heart disease; heart failure; heart block.

hfref: Structural heart disease / low EF: harmful.

preg.text: May be considered in pregnancy (2 mg/kg over 10 min) for stable AF.

src: ESC24-AF|Pharmacological cardioversion with flecainide (no structural heart disease)
ESC19-SVT|Pre-excited AF: flecainide may be considered (IIb)
flecainide_iv.check: Second check: the IV form is not in the US label; BNF check pending. Often not available in Pakistan.
flecainide_iv.name: Flecainide IV (no structural heart disease only)

mag_tdp.how: Over 10 minutes (RCUK). Correct potassium to 4.5-5.0 mmol/L as well. In cardiac arrest from torsades, defibrillate first: magnesium does not replace shocks.
mag_tdp.max: May repeat once; watch reflexes and breathing.
mag_tdp.watch: Flushing, low BP, slow breathing in kidney failure.

ckd: Kidney failure: magnesium builds up; watch reflexes and breathing.

preg.text: Used in pregnancy.

src: RCUK25|Adult tachyarrhythmia algorithm v3 2026: torsades: magnesium 8 mmol IV over 10 min; avoid amiodarone
AHA25-ALS|Section 16 Rec 2: magnesium may be considered for recurrent torsades with a long QT
mag_tdp.check: LABEL: no torsades dose in the label; 2 g = 8 mmol (agrees with RCUK). BNF check pending.
mag_tdp.name: Magnesium sulfate (torsades de pointes)

isoprenaline.how: Titrate to heart rate (bradycardia; or torsades that comes with a slow rate).
isoprenaline.contra: Congenital long QT (torsades): use only on expert advice; ischaemia.
src: RCUK25|Adult bradyarrhythmia algorithm 2025 (isoprenaline 5 micrograms/min); tachyarrhythmia algorithm (isoprenaline or pacing for torsades)
isoprenaline.check: LABEL (heart block): initial 5 micrograms/min IV (agrees). Often not available in Pakistan.
isoprenaline.name: Isoprenaline (isoproterenol) infusion

atropine.watch: Dry mouth, confusion in the elderly, tachycardia.
atropine.cautions: Often does not work in Mobitz II or complete heart block with wide QRS, or after a heart transplant: do not delay pacing. Avoid in acute ischaemia if it would speed the heart too much.
atropine.contra: None in symptomatic bradycardia (glaucoma is relative).

preg.text: Can be used in pregnancy for unstable bradycardia.
src: ESC25-PREG|§12.4.4: do not withhold resuscitation drugs
AHA25-ALS|Bradycardia algorithm 2025, Doses/Details: 1 mg bolus, repeat every 3-5 min, max 3 mg
RCUK25|Adult bradyarrhythmia 2025: 500 micrograms, repeat to 3 mg
atropine.check: LABEL: 0.4-1 mg IV, up to 2 mg; the resuscitation guidelines allow up to 3 mg.
atropine.diff: AHA 2025: 1 mg per dose. RCUK / ERC 2025: 500 micrograms per dose. Both: maximum 3 mg. The app shows the AHA dose.
atropine.name: Atropine

epi_inf.how: Example: 1 mg in 100 mL saline = 10 micrograms/mL; 2-10 micrograms/min = 12-60 mL/hour. Titrate to heart rate and BP.
epi_inf.watch: Tachycardia, arrhythmia, ischaemia; tissue damage if it leaks.
epi_inf.name: Epinephrine (adrenaline) infusion

dopamine.how: Start at 5 and titrate; taper slowly when stopping.
dopamine.max: 20 micrograms/kg/min (switch to norepinephrine for low BP if more is needed).
dopamine.watch: Tachycardia, arrhythmia; tissue damage if it leaks.
dopamine.contra: Untreated low volume (give fluid first); pheochromocytoma.
dopamine.check: LABEL: 2-50 micrograms/kg/min for shock; if low BP persists, change to a stronger vasoconstrictor (agrees with the 5-20 range).
dopamine.name: Dopamine infusion

aspirin.route: By mouth, chewed (IV 75-250 mg if cannot swallow)
aspirin.how: Give at once once dissection is not suspected.
aspirin.contra: True aspirin allergy; active major bleeding; suspected aortic dissection.

preg.text: Low-dose aspirin is safe in pregnancy; give the loading dose for ACS.

src: ESC23-ACS|Doses table: aspirin loading 150-300 mg orally or 75-250 mg IV
aspirin.check: LABEL (clopidogrel / ticagrelor pages): aspirin 75-325 mg daily; with ticagrelor keep the daily aspirin 75-100 mg.
aspirin.diff: The two guidelines differ slightly in the loading dose: ESC 150-300 mg, ACC/AHA 162-325 mg. 300 mg fits both.
aspirin.name: Aspirin (loading)

clopidogrel_lysis.how: Give with aspirin at the time of fibrinolysis.

age75: Over 75: 75 mg only, no 300 mg loading.

preg.text: May be used in pregnancy when needed (short time); stop at least 5 days before neuraxial anaesthesia.

src: ESC23-ACS|Doses table: clopidogrel with fibrinolysis 300 mg (75 mg if over 75 years)
clopidogrel_lysis.check: LABEL: STEMI 300 mg loading optional, then 75 mg daily with or without fibrinolytics; no age note in the label.
clopidogrel_lysis.diff: The label does not give the over-75 rule; the ESC table does (75 mg).
clopidogrel_lysis.name: Clopidogrel with fibrinolysis

src: ESC23-ACS|Doses table: clopidogrel 300-600 mg loading (600 mg for PCI)
clopidogrel_pci.check: LABEL: 300 mg loading in ACS (the 600 mg PCI loading is from the guidelines).
clopidogrel_pci.diff: ESC 2023: routine pretreatment before primary PCI may be considered (IIb); give the P2Y12 drug NICVD's team asks for.
clopidogrel_pci.name: Clopidogrel before primary PCI (only if NICVD asks, or ticagrelor is not available)

ticagrelor.how: Keep daily aspirin at 75-100 mg (more aspirin weakens ticagrelor).
ticagrelor.contra: Previous brain bleed; active bleeding; with fibrinolysis (use clopidogrel instead).
src: ESC23-ACS|Doses table: ticagrelor 180 mg loading, 90 mg twice daily
ticagrelor.check: LABEL: 180 mg loading, 90 mg twice daily for a year; aspirin 75-100 mg (agrees).
ticagrelor.name: Ticagrelor (before primary PCI, if NICVD asks)

tenecteplase.how: Flush the line with saline before and after (it precipitates with glucose). Age 75 or more: give HALF the weight dose (ESC 2023). Start within 10 minutes of the STEMI diagnosis.
tenecteplase.watch: Bleeding (gums, puncture sites, urine, brain: sudden headache, drowsiness, weakness), reperfusion arrhythmias, low BP.
tenecteplase.contra: See the thrombolysis checklist (absolute and relative contraindications).

preg.text: Pregnancy is a relative contraindication: primary PCI is preferred; fibrinolysis only if timely PCI is not possible.

src: ESC23-ACS|Doses of fibrinolytic agents (weight bands; half dose at 75 years or more)
tenecteplase.check: LABEL: the same weight bands, single bolus over 5 s; flush dextrose lines (agrees). MCMASTER table: same bands. The half dose at 75 years or more is from the ESC 2023 table: please confirm it there.
tenecteplase.name: Tenecteplase (fibrinolysis for STEMI)

alteplase_mi.how: Over 67 kg: 15 mg, then 50 mg over 30 min, then 35 mg over 60 min.

preg.text: Relative contraindication in pregnancy; it does not cross the placenta but can cause bleeding.

alteplase_mi.check: LABEL: 15 mg, then 0.75 mg/kg (max 50) over 30 min, then 0.5 mg/kg (max 35) over 60 min; total 100 mg (agrees).
alteplase_mi.name: Alteplase (fibrinolysis for STEMI, accelerated 90-minute regimen)

reteplase.check: LABEL: 10 units over 2 min, repeated after 30 min (agrees).
reteplase.name: Reteplase (fibrinolysis for STEMI)

streptokinase.route: IV infusion in 100 mL 0.9% saline or 5% glucose
streptokinase.how: Not if streptokinase was given before (antibodies make it fail and cause reactions). Low BP during the infusion: slow it down and raise the legs.
streptokinase.contra: Previous streptokinase; see the thrombolysis checklist.
src: ESC23-ACS|Doses of fibrinolytic agents (streptokinase 1.5 million IU over 30-60 min)
streptokinase.check: MCMASTER table: 1.5 million IU in 100 mL over 30-60 min (agrees). Not sold in the US, so no US label.
streptokinase.name: Streptokinase (fibrinolysis for STEMI)

ufh_lysis.how: For 24-48 hours. aPTT 50-70 seconds (1.5-2 times control) at 3, 6, 12 and 24 hours.
ufh_lysis.contra: Active bleeding; suspected aortic dissection; previous heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.

preg.text: Heparin does not cross the placenta; safe in pregnancy.

src: ESC23-ACS|Doses table: UFH with fibrinolysis 60 IU/kg (max 4000) then 12 IU/kg/h (max 1000), aPTT 50-70 s, 24-48 h
ufh_lysis.check: MCMASTER table: the same doses and aPTT target (agrees).
ufh_lysis.diff: ESC 2023 prefers enoxaparin over UFH with fibrinolysis; UFH is first here because it is the CEC's usual anticoagulant when available.
ufh_lysis.name: Unfractionated heparin with fibrinolysis (the CEC's usual anticoagulant)

doses: 30 mg IV, then 15 min later 1 mg/kg SC every 12 h (max 100 mg for the first 2 doses)
No IV dose; 0.75 mg/kg SC every 12 h (max 75 mg for the first 2 doses)
Same doses but once every 24 h
enox_lysis.how: Until revascularisation or hospital discharge (up to 8 days).

age75: 75 or over: no IV bolus, 0.75 mg/kg.
ckd: CrCl below 30: once daily; below 15 use UFH.

preg.text: LMWH is safe in pregnancy.

enox_lysis.check: LABEL: STEMI with fibrinolysis: 30 mg IV + 1 mg/kg SC, then 1 mg/kg every 12 h (max 100 mg first 2 doses); 75 or over 0.75 mg/kg (max 75); CrCl < 30 once daily (agrees). MCMASTER table agrees.
enox_lysis.name: Enoxaparin with fibrinolysis

fonda_lysis.contra: CrCl below 30 (label); not alone for primary PCI.
src: ESC23-ACS|Doses table: fondaparinux 2.5 mg IV then 2.5 mg SC daily (with streptokinase)

fonda_lysis.name: Fondaparinux with fibrinolysis (with streptokinase)

ufh_nste.contra: Active bleeding; suspected aortic dissection; previous HIT.

preg.text: Safe in pregnancy.

src: ESC23-ACS|Doses table: UFH in NSTE-ACS (medical treatment) 60-70 IU/kg, max 5000, then 12-15 IU/kg/h, max 1000
ufh_nste.check: Second check: pending (BNF). The doses are the long-standing ESC NSTE-ACS table values.

enox_nste.how: For at least 2 days, until stable.

preg.text: Safe in pregnancy.

fonda_nste.how: If the patient goes for PCI, the PCI team adds UFH.

src: ESC23-ACS|Doses table: fondaparinux 2.5 mg SC daily (preferred by ESC when no early invasive strategy)

ufh_pci.how: Write the dose and time on the referral.

ufh_pci.name: Unfractionated heparin before primary PCI (ONLY if NICVD asks for it before transfer)

doses: 0.3 to 0.6 mg (one tablet or one spray of 0.4 mg)
gtn_sl.how: Every 5 minutes for ongoing pain, up to 3 doses. Sitting or lying.
gtn_sl.contra: SBP below 90; right ventricular infarction (inferior STEMI with right-sided ST elevation); sildenafil or vardenafil in the last 24 h, tadalafil in the last 48 h; severe aortic stenosis.

preg.text: Can be used in pregnancy (watch BP).

gtn_sl.check: LABEL: 0.3-0.6 mg sublingually every 5 min, at most 3 doses in 15 min (agrees).
gtn_sl.name: Glyceryl trinitrate (nitroglycerin) under the tongue

gtn_iv.route: IV infusion (glass or non-PVC set if available)
gtn_iv.how: Example: 50 mg in 50 mL = 1 mg/mL; 10 micrograms/min = 0.6 mL/hour. Pulmonary oedema: raise quickly while SBP stays above 110.
gtn_iv.watch: Low BP, headache, tolerance after 24 h.
gtn_iv.contra: SBP below 90 (below 110 in acute heart failure); right ventricular infarction; recent sildenafil / tadalafil; severe aortic stenosis.

preg.text: Pulmonary oedema with pre-eclampsia: start 5 micrograms/min, up to 100 micrograms/min, with diuretics.

src: ESC26-HF|Section 7, Figure 13: vasodilators when SBP > 110 mmHg
gtn_iv.check: LABEL: start 5 micrograms/min, +5 every 3-5 min to 20, then +10 to 20; no fixed maximum (agrees).
gtn_iv.name: Glyceryl trinitrate (nitroglycerin) infusion

morphine.how: Repeat every 5-15 minutes if needed; give an anti-sickness drug.
morphine.watch: Low BP, slow breathing, vomiting; it slows the absorption of oral P2Y12 drugs.
src: ESC23-ACS|Titrated IV opioids may be considered for severe pain (IIb)
ESC26-HF|Opioids not routinely used in decompensated HF
morphine.name: Morphine (severe pain or distress)

doses: IV dose = about 2 times the usual daily oral dose
furosemide.how: Check urine output (aim more than 100-150 mL/hour in the first 6 hours) and, if possible, urine sodium at 2 hours.
furosemide.watch: Low potassium and sodium, low BP, kidney function.
furosemide.contra: No urine at all (anuria) without dialysis plan; severe low volume.

preg.text: Use for pulmonary oedema in pregnancy (it may reduce placental blood flow; avoid in pre-eclampsia unless pulmonary oedema).

src: ESC26-HF|Section 7, Figure 13: IV loop diuretic (40 mg furosemide if diuretic-naive, or double the daily oral dose in chronic users)
furosemide.check: LABEL: acute pulmonary oedema 40 mg IV over 1-2 min, 80 mg if no response within 1 hour (agrees).
furosemide.name: Furosemide IV

norepinephrine.route: IV infusion, central line if possible
norepinephrine.how: Target MAP 65 mmHg or more. Example: 4 mg in 50 mL = 80 micrograms/mL.
norepinephrine.watch: Ischaemia of fingers and gut; tissue damage if it leaks; arrhythmia.
norepinephrine.contra: Untreated low volume (give fluid if no congestion).
src: AHA25-PCAC|Section 5: MAP of at least 65 mmHg after ROSC
norepinephrine.check: LABEL: start 8-12 micrograms/min, maintain 2-4 micrograms/min, titrate to low-normal BP; septic shock 0.01-3 micrograms/kg/min (consistent).
norepinephrine.name: Norepinephrine (noradrenaline) infusion

dobutamine.how: For low output with adequate BP (it can lower BP); combine with norepinephrine if BP is low.
src: ESC26-HF|Section 7: inotropes in low output with hypoperfusion
dobutamine.name: Dobutamine infusion

doses: 80 mg IV (300 mg in total at most)
labetalol.how: Lying down. BP every 5 minutes. Stop at the target; then oral treatment.
labetalol.watch: Low BP on standing, slow heart rate, wheeze.
labetalol.contra: Asthma or COPD with wheeze; heart block; acute heart failure; slow heart rate; cocaine / amphetamine crisis (unopposed alpha) is debated.

hfref: Avoid in acute decompensated heart failure.

preg.text: First-line IV drug for severe hypertension in pregnancy (20 mg, then 40, then 80 every 10 min; max 300 mg).

src: ESC19-HTNEM|Labetalol first-line in several hypertensive emergencies (0.25-0.5 mg/kg; 2-4 mg/min until goal, then 5-20 mg/h)
