labetalol.name: Labetalol IV

nicardipine.how: At the goal, lower to about 3 mg/hour.

preg.text: An IV option in pregnancy (ESC 2025: IV labetalol or nicardipine).

nicardipine.check: LABEL: start 5 mg/h, +2.5 mg/h every 5-15 min, max 15 mg/h, then 3 mg/h (agrees). Often not available in Pakistan.
nicardipine.name: Nicardipine infusion

preg.text: ESC 2025: an option in pregnancy where available.

urapidil.check: Not in the US label (not sold there); BNF check pending.
urapidil.name: Urapidil IV

nitroprusside.route: IV infusion, protected from light, arterial line ideally
nitroprusside.watch: Sudden low BP; cyanide toxicity with long use or kidney failure.

preg.text: Last resort in pregnancy (cyanide risk to the baby).

nitroprusside.name: Sodium nitroprusside infusion (ICU only)

hydralazine.how: Recheck BP in 20 minutes. If 20 mg in total has not worked, change to labetalol (ACOG).
hydralazine.watch: Low BP, fast heart rate, headache; foetal heart rate changes.

preg.text: ESC 2025: second-line (less effective, more side effects than labetalol or nifedipine).

src: ACOG767|Hydralazine 5-10 mg IV over 2 min, repeat in 20 min
hydralazine.check: LABEL: 20-40 mg IM or IV for severe hypertension outside pregnancy; the small pregnancy doses are from ACOG.
hydralazine.name: Hydralazine IV (pregnancy, second-line)

doses: Repeat after 20-30 min if still 160/110 or more
nifedipine_po.route: By mouth: swallow; never bite a capsule or put it under the tongue
nifedipine_po.how: Continuous foetal monitoring if viable. Outside pregnancy, do not use short-acting nifedipine for high BP (sudden falls, stroke).
nifedipine_po.watch: Headache, flushing, fast fall in BP (especially with magnesium).
nifedipine_po.contra: Outside pregnancy: not for hypertensive emergency.

preg.text: ESC 2025: oral nifedipine, labetalol or methyldopa for severe hypertension; nifedipine was better in some studies.

nifedipine_po.check: Two sources: ESC 2025 (10 mg) and ACOG (10 mg, then 20 mg).
nifedipine_po.name: Nifedipine by mouth (pregnancy)

doses: 4 g IV slowly (label: 4 g diluted to 10-20% over 3-4 minutes, or 4-5 g in 250 mL)
mgso4_eclampsia.how: Before each dose and every hour: knee reflexes present, breathing 16 per minute or more, urine at least 100 mL in 4 hours (label). Toxicity: stop it and give calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL IV (ESC 2025).
mgso4_eclampsia.max: Kidney failure: lower infusion and check levels.
mgso4_eclampsia.watch: Loss of reflexes, slow breathing, low BP.

ckd: Builds up in kidney failure: lower infusion, check levels.

preg.text: The drug for pre-eclampsia with severe features (to prevent fits), alongside delivery planning.

src: ESC25-PREG|§12.3.3.2 magnesium sulfate for pre-eclampsia with severe features; toxicity: calcium gluconate 30 mL
mgso4_eclampsia.check: LABEL: loading 4-5 g IV, maintenance 1-2 g/h, up to 30-40 g/day; calcium salt ready (agrees).
mgso4_eclampsia.name: Magnesium sulfate (severe pre-eclampsia / eclampsia)

vagal.name: Vagal manoeuvre (modified Valsalva)
vagal.text: Patient semi-sitting blows into a 10 mL syringe (or hard against closed lips) for 15 seconds, then is laid flat at once with the legs lifted to 45 degrees for 15 seconds. Run a rhythm strip. Carotid massage only if no bruit and no stroke history. Never press on the eyes.

sync_cv.name: Synchronised cardioversion
sync_cv.text: Sedate whenever possible (the doctor who sedates manages the airway). Pads front-and-side or front-and-back. Press SYNC and check the markers on each QRS; re-press SYNC after each shock. Energy (AHA 2025 electrical cardioversion algorithm, biphasic): AF 200 J; flutter 200 J; regular narrow tachycardia 100 J; monomorphic VT 100 J; increase if it fails (up to 3 attempts, RCUK). Follow your defibrillator's guide; if unknown, use the maximum. Polymorphic VT: NOT synchronised: defibrillate. In pregnancy: safe at every stage, same energy; monitor the baby afterwards.
src: AHA25-ALS|Electrical Cardioversion Algorithm 2025 and Section 18.1 (200 J for AF / flutter)

defib.name: Unsynchronised shock (defibrillation)
defib.text: For polymorphic VT (always unstable) and pulseless rhythms: defibrillate at once with the device's defibrillation dose (biphasic 120-200 J as the maker advises, or the maximum; monophasic 360 J). If the pulse is lost, start CPR and use Code mode.
src: AHA25-ALS|Top message 8: polymorphic VT needs immediate defibrillation; Cardiac arrest algorithm shock energy

tcp.name: Transcutaneous pacing
tcp.text: Pads front and back. Demand mode, rate 60-70/min; raise the current until every spike is followed by a wide QRS (electrical capture), then check a pulse for mechanical capture; set 5-10 mA above the threshold. Give pain relief and sedation. Arrange transvenous pacing (refer to NICVD).
src: AHA25-ALS|Bradycardia algorithm 2025: transcutaneous pacing if atropine fails; consider transvenous pacing
RCUK25|Adult bradyarrhythmia 2025: transcutaneous pacing; seek expert help

nondrug_rate.name: No drug available: synchronised cardioversion or referral
nondrug_rate.text: If the patient becomes unstable: synchronised cardioversion. If stable: keep monitored, treat the cause (fever, low volume, low oxygen, thyroid, pain) and refer to the cardiologist / NICVD.
src: AHA25-ALS|Tachyarrhythmia algorithm: if refractory, expert consultation

nondrug_apo.name: Without drugs
nondrug_apo.text: Sit the patient upright with legs down. Oxygen if SpO2 below 90%; CPAP / non-invasive ventilation if breathless (RR over 25) and SpO2 below 90%. Urgent referral to a CCU (NICVD).
src: ESC26-HF|Section 7, Figure 13: oxygen, non-invasive ventilation, early transfer

pressor_none.name: No vasopressor available
pressor_none.text: Lay flat with legs raised, fluid bolus 200-250 mL over 15-30 minutes if no congestion, treat the cause (STEMI: urgent PCI), and transfer to NICVD at once with a doctor.
src: ESC26-HF|Cardiogenic shock: early transfer to a centre with a Shock Team

bp_none.name: No IV antihypertensive available
bp_none.text: Treat the cause and the organ damage, keep the patient lying down and calm, avoid fast falls (never sublingual nifedipine capsules outside pregnancy), and transfer to an ICU with titratable IV drugs (NICVD for aortic dissection, a stroke centre for stroke).
src: AHAACC25-HBP|Section 6.2: ICU admission for hypertensive emergency
ESC24-HTN|Hypertensive emergencies: titratable IV drugs in a monitored setting

tdp_care.name: Torsades: correct the causes
tdp_care.text: Potassium to 4.5-5.0 mmol/L, magnesium normal, stop every QT-lengthening drug, treat slow heart rate. Defibrillate any sustained run. Do not give amiodarone.
src: ESC22-VA|Torsades: correct electrolytes, withdraw offending drugs

dialysis.name: Dialysis / referral
dialysis.text: Severe hyperkalaemia that does not settle: urgent dialysis. Arrange transfer while continuing treatment.
src: RCUK25-SPEC|Consider dialysis for refractory severe hyperkalaemia

refer_nicvd.name: Refer to NICVD Karachi
refer_nicvd.text: Call NICVD (emergency / cath lab) and the ambulance. Send the ECGs, this record and the drugs given (with times). Transfer with a doctor, monitor, defibrillator and oxygen.
src: ACCAHA25-ACS|Systems of care: transfer for PCI

refer_expert.name: Call the senior / cardiologist and refer
refer_expert.text: Get expert help now: the CEC senior / cardiologist on call; transfer to NICVD if the rhythm or condition does not settle.

refer_obs.name: Obstetric emergency referral
refer_obs.text: Call the obstetrician now and transfer to a hospital with obstetric and neonatal cover, with the drugs given written down. Continuous foetal monitoring.
src: ESC25-PREG|Pregnancy Heart Team; §12.3.3 severe hypertension: admission

hst.title: Reversible causes (Hs and Ts)
src: AHA25-ALS|Adult Cardiac Arrest Algorithm: reversible causes
items: Oxygen, airway position, tube in the right place (capnography).
Diabetic ketoacidosis, kidney failure, long arrest.
Dialysis patient? Wide QRS, peaked T: calcium, insulin with glucose, bicarbonate.
Trauma, ventilated, one side not moving: needle decompression.
Raised neck veins, after trauma or surgery: echo; pericardiocentesis.
Sudden breathlessness before collapse, leg swelling: consider fibrinolysis.
Chest pain before the arrest: after ROSC, ECG and PCI.

lysis_cx.title: Fibrinolysis: contraindications

groups.rel: Relative: weigh benefit against bleeding (senior decision)

items: Any previous brain bleed, or a stroke of unknown cause
Ischaemic stroke in the last 6 months
Brain or spinal damage, tumour or vascular malformation
Major trauma, surgery or head injury in the last month
Bleeding from the gut in the last month
Known bleeding disorder or active bleeding (not menses)
Puncture that cannot be pressed in the last 24 hours (e.g. liver biopsy, lumbar puncture)
Pregnant or within 1 week after delivery
BP above 180/110 that does not come down
lysis_cx.note: ACC/AHA lists ischaemic stroke within 3 months as absolute (ESC: 6 months). The stricter ESC limit is used here (safer).

redflags.title: Chest pain: red flags for other killers
src: ESC23-ACS|Differential diagnosis of acute chest pain
items: Sudden, severe, tearing or ripping pain, often to the back
Pulse or BP difference between arms (more than 20 mmHg) or a missing pulse
New aortic regurgitation murmur, or stroke signs with the pain
Marfan, known aortic aneurysm or aortic valve disease
Breathlessness with a clear chest, low SpO2, fast heart rate
Swollen tender calf, recent surgery, bed rest, cancer or pregnancy
Coughing blood, or previous DVT / PE
Low BP with raised neck veins and soft heart sounds
BP falls more than 10 mmHg on breathing in (pulsus paradoxus)
Low-voltage ECG or alternating QRS size; fluid around the heart on echo

rosc.title: After ROSC: checklist
items: Airway secure; waveform capnography; breathe 10 per minute
Oxygen: 100% until SpO2 can be measured, then SpO2 90-98%
BP: MAP 65 mmHg or more (fluids, norepinephrine)
STEMI: emergency PCI (refer to NICVD), even if comatose.
Shock without STEMI: urgent angiography is reasonable
Temperature control 32-37.5 C for at least 36 hours; prevent fever
AHA 2025 section 7 (ERC: prevent fever above 37.7 C for 72 h).
Treat fits; EEG if not obeying commands
Find and treat the cause (Hs and Ts)
Transfer to ICU / CCU with a doctor (NICVD for PCI)

tod.title: Acute organ damage from high BP

groups.enc: Encephalopathy / malignant hypertension / acute kidney injury

items: Tearing chest or back pain, pulse difference
Ischaemic chest pain or new ischaemic ECG
New weakness, speech or face problem (stroke)
Confusion, fits, severe headache with vomiting
Sudden loss of vision, retinal bleeding or papilloedema
Falling urine, rising creatinine, blood in urine
Cocaine / amphetamine, or pheochromocytoma attacks (headache, sweating, palpitations)

vf.name: Ventricular fibrillation (VF)
vf.text: Chaotic waves of varying size, no QRS complexes, no pulse.

pvt.name: Pulseless ventricular tachycardia
pvt.text: Wide regular QRS complexes with no pulse: treat exactly as VF (shock).

asys.name: Asystole
asys.text: A flat line. Check leads, gain and pads before calling it; look for P waves (P-wave asystole may respond to pacing).

pea.name: Pulseless electrical activity (PEA)
pea.text: An organised rhythm on the monitor but no pulse. Look hard for a reversible cause (Hs and Ts).
src: AHA25-ALS|Adult Cardiac Arrest Algorithm: reversible causes

sinus_t.name: Sinus tachycardia
sinus_t.text: Normal P waves before each QRS, normal PR; the rate rose gradually and changes with the cause (fever, pain, low volume, low oxygen, anaemia, PE, thyroid, anxiety).
src: RCUK25|Tachyarrhythmia algorithm note: in sinus tachycardia treat the cause

fat.name: Focal atrial tachycardia
fat.text: A P wave before each QRS but with an abnormal shape or axis (e.g. upside-down in II), regular, often 120-220/min. Adenosine may stop it or only block the AV node for a moment (the P waves go on).

flutter.name: Atrial flutter
flutter.text: Saw-tooth flutter waves (best in II, III, aVF, V1), atrial rate about 300; with 2:1 block the heart rate is about 150. Treat like AF (rate control, anticoagulation, cardioversion 200 J).

flutter_v.name: Atrial flutter with varying block
flutter_v.text: Flutter waves with an irregular ventricular rate. Treat like AF.

avnrt.name: AV nodal re-entrant tachycardia (AVNRT)
avnrt.text: Regular narrow tachycardia (often 140-250), sudden start; P waves hidden in the QRS or a small notch at its end (pseudo r' in V1). The commonest SVT.

avrt.name: AV re-entrant tachycardia (AVRT, accessory pathway / WPW)
avrt.text: Regular narrow tachycardia with an upside-down P wave clearly after the QRS (RP interval about 70 ms or more). In sinus rhythm there may be a delta wave (WPW). Acute treatment is the same as AVNRT.

nrt.name: Regular narrow-complex tachycardia (SVT, type not clear yet)
nrt.text: Treated the same way first (vagal manoeuvre, adenosine). Adenosine on a rhythm strip often shows the type.
src: ESC19-SVT|Acute management of regular narrow QRS tachycardia

af.name: Atrial fibrillation (AF)
af.text: Irregularly irregular narrow QRS, no P waves, wavy or flat baseline.

af_bbb.name: AF with bundle branch block
af_bbb.text: Irregular wide QRS with the SAME shape every beat (typical bundle branch block). Treat as AF; if the QRS shape varies and some beats are very close, think of pre-excited AF.
src: ESC24-AF|AF with aberrant conduction (rate and rhythm control as for AF)

mat.name: Multifocal atrial tachycardia (MAT)
mat.text: Irregular narrow rhythm over 100 with P waves of 3 or more shapes and varying PR. Usually lung disease, low oxygen or low potassium / magnesium.

sinus_ect.name: Sinus tachycardia with ectopic beats
sinus_ect.text: Normal P waves with some early beats. Treat the cause.

vt.name: Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia (treat any regular wide tachycardia as VT)
vt.text: Regular wide QRS (0.12 s or more), the same shape each beat. AV dissociation, capture or fusion beats, very wide QRS or old MI make VT almost certain. If unsure: VT.

svt_ab.name: SVT with known bundle branch block (aberrancy)
svt_ab.text: Only when an old ECG shows the same QRS shape in sinus rhythm. Treat as SVT (vagal, adenosine); if anything does not fit, treat as VT.
src: RCUK25|Known SVT with aberrant conduction: treat as narrow regular
AHA25-ALS|Section 15 (adenosine only if regular and monomorphic)

pxaf.name: Pre-excited atrial fibrillation (AF with WPW)
pxaf.text: Very fast irregular wide QRS (often over 200) whose shape changes from beat to beat, with some very short RR intervals; often a young patient. AV-node blockers can cause VF.
src: AHA25-ALS|Section 18.2 Rec 3 (harm from AV-nodal blockers and IV amiodarone)

tdp.name: Torsades de pointes (polymorphic VT with long QT)
tdp.text: QRS complexes that twist around the baseline, with a long QT on the beats before. Often drugs, low potassium or magnesium, or slow heart rate.

pmvt.name: Polymorphic VT with a normal QT
pmvt.text: Twisting QRS with a normal QT: usually acute ischaemia.

pvt_unk.name: Polymorphic VT (QT not known)
pvt_unk.text: Treat the rhythm first (defibrillate); magnesium is low-risk; check the QT once the rhythm settles.
src: AHA25-ALS|Top message 8: polymorphic VT needs immediate defibrillation

nsr.name: Sinus rhythm (no arrhythmia)
nsr.text: Normal P before every QRS, PR 0.12-0.20 s, rate 50-100.

sb.name: Sinus bradycardia
sb.text: Normal P before every QRS, rate under 50. Common in fit people and in sleep; also drugs, low thyroid, inferior MI, raised brain pressure.

avb1.name: First-degree AV block
avb1.text: Every P is followed by a QRS but the PR is longer than 0.20 s.

mob1.name: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz I (Wenckebach)
mob1.text: The PR gets longer and longer until a P wave is not conducted; then it starts again. Usually at the AV node; often benign.

mob2.name: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz II (or 2:1 block)
mob2.text: Some P waves are not conducted with a constant PR before them (or every second P is blocked). Risk of sudden complete block / asystole.

chb.name: Complete (third-degree) heart block, narrow escape
chb.text: P waves and QRS are unrelated; more P waves than QRS; regular narrow escape rhythm (junctional).

chb_w.name: Complete heart block with a wide (ventricular) escape
chb_w.text: P waves and QRS unrelated; slow wide escape rhythm. High risk of asystole; atropine rarely works.
src: RCUK25|Bradyarrhythmia: complete heart block with broad QRS = risk of asystole

junc.name: Junctional rhythm
junc.text: Regular narrow QRS without P waves before it (P may be hidden or just after the QRS); escape rate 40-60, accelerated 60-100.
src: ESC21-PACE|Sinus node and AV conduction disorders

idio.name: Ventricular escape (idioventricular) rhythm
idio.text: Very slow (20-40) wide QRS without P waves. High risk of asystole.

af_slow.name: AF with a slow ventricular rate
af_slow.text: Irregular QRS without P waves, rate under 50: drugs (beta-blocker, calcium blocker, digoxin), conduction disease.
src: ESC24-AF|Rate control drugs as a cause of slow AF

af_ctrl.name: AF with a controlled rate
af_ctrl.text: Irregular narrow QRS without P waves, rate 50-100.
src: ESC24-AF|Diagnosis of AF; rate control target

stemi.name: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)
stemi.text: Ischaemic symptoms with new ST elevation at the J point in 2 neighbouring leads: 1 mm or more in all leads except V2-V3, where it is 2 mm or more in men 40 or over, 2.5 mm in men under 40, 1.5 mm in women. Equivalents: posterior MI (ST depression V1-V3 with ST elevation in V7-V9), new LBBB or paced rhythm with ongoing ischaemia.
src: ESC23-ACS|ECG criteria for STEMI and STEMI equivalents

preg.label: Pregnant, or delivered in the last 6 weeks?

ckd.label: Kidney function poor (eGFR or CrCl below 30, or on dialysis)

lqt.label: Long QT (known, QTc over 500 ms now, or on QT-lengthening drugs)

hfref.label: Heart failure with low EF (LVEF 40% or less) or acute heart failure now

dx.title: Rhythm diagnosis
dx.sub: From the very start: pulse, rate, QRS, regularity, P waves, QT

d_pulse.text: Check for a pulse and normal breathing (no more than 10 seconds). Is there a pulse?
ans: No pulse, or not breathing normally

d_nopulse.warn: Chest compressions: 100-120 per minute, at least 5 cm deep, full recoil.
d_nopulse.text: Start CPR now. What does the monitor show?
ans: Wide regular QRS but no pulse (pulseless VT)
A rhythm with QRS complexes but no pulse (PEA)
src: AHA25-ALS|Adult Cardiac Arrest Algorithm (shockable or not)

d_rate.help: A tachyarrhythmia that causes symptoms is usually 150 or more; under 150 look hard for a cause.
src: AHA25-ALS|Bradycardia algorithm (typically under 50) and Tachyarrhythmia algorithm (typically 150 or more)

d_fast.text: Is the patient unstable because of the fast rhythm? Low BP or shock, fainting, ischaemic chest pain, acute heart failure, or confused.

src: AHA25-ALS|Tachyarrhythmia algorithm: wide QRS 0.12 s or more

d_nrp.help: Adenosine on a rhythm strip can unmask flutter waves or atrial tachycardia.
d_nrp.text: Look at the P waves (lead II and V1). What do you see?
ans: Normal P before each QRS; the rate rose gradually (usually under 150)
A P before each QRS, but an abnormal shape (e.g. upside-down in II)
No P wave seen, or a small notch at the very end of the QRS
An upside-down P clearly after the QRS, in the ST segment
src: ESC19-SVT|Differential diagnosis of narrow QRS tachycardia (P-wave position)

d_nip.text: P waves in the irregular narrow rhythm?
ans: No P waves; wavy or flat baseline
P waves of 3 or more shapes, the PR varies
Normal P waves with some early beats

src: RCUK25|Tachyarrhythmia algorithm: broad QRS, is it regular?

d_wr.help: Features of VT: P waves marching through (AV dissociation), capture or fusion beats, QRS over 0.16 s, extreme axis, old MI or heart disease.
d_wr.text: Wide and regular. Is it clearly a known bundle branch block from an old ECG with exactly the same QRS shape?
ans: No, or not sure: treat as VT
Yes: same QRS shape as the old ECG
src: ESC22-VA|Wide QRS tachycardia: treat as VT unless proven otherwise
RCUK25|Broad regular: treat as VT; known aberrancy: treat as narrow

d_wip.text: Wide and irregular. What does the QRS look like?
ans: Each QRS a different size and direction, twisting around the line (polymorphic)
Very fast (often over 200), the shape changes, some beats very close together (young, or known WPW)
The same wide shape every beat, rhythm irregular
src: RCUK25|Broad irregular: AF with BBB, pre-excited AF, polymorphic VT

d_qt.help: QT-lengthening drugs include many antibiotics (azithromycin, levofloxacin), ondansetron, haloperidol, antimalarials and some antiarrhythmics.
d_qt.text: Before the attack (or between runs) is the QT long (QTc over 500 ms), or is the patient on QT-lengthening drugs or low in potassium / magnesium?
src: ESC22-VA|Torsades de pointes vs polymorphic VT with normal QT

d_norm.text: Relation of the P waves to the QRS?
ans: A normal P before every QRS, PR 0.12-0.20 s
A P before every QRS, PR longer than 0.20 s
Some P waves not followed by a QRS; the PR lengthens before the dropped beat
Some P waves not followed by a QRS; the PR stays the same
P waves and QRS unrelated (more P waves than QRS)
No P waves, regular narrow QRS
src: ESC21-PACE|Classification of AV block and sinus node disease

d_nsr_end.text: No arrhythmia on this ECG. Look for the cause of the symptoms; repeat the ECG if they come back.

d_slow.text: Is the slow rhythm causing danger signs? Shock or low BP, fainting, ischaemic chest pain, heart failure.

d_sp.text: Relation of the P waves to the QRS?
ans: A normal P before every QRS, normal PR
A P before every QRS, PR longer than 0.20 s
Some P waves blocked; the PR lengthens before the dropped beat
Some P waves blocked; the PR stays the same (or 2:1)
P waves and QRS unrelated; regular slow QRS
No P waves, narrow QRS (or P just after the QRS)
No P waves, wide QRS, very slow (20-40)

d_chbq.text: Complete heart block: is the escape QRS narrow or wide?
src: RCUK25|Complete heart block with broad QRS: risk of asystole

tachy.title: Tachycardia with a pulse
tachy.sub: Stable or unstable; drugs with alternatives; synchronised cardioversion

t_stab.help: Sinus tachycardia from another illness is not treated with cardioversion.
t_stab.text: Unstable because of the tachycardia? Low BP or shock, fainting, ischaemic chest pain, acute heart failure, confused.

ans: I need help reading the rhythm
Very fast, the QRS shape varies (pre-excited AF)
The same wide shape each beat (AF with bundle branch block)

src: AHA25-ALS|Tachyarrhythmia algorithm box 6 and Electrical Cardioversion algorithm (narrow complex 100 J)
RCUK25|Unstable: synchronised shock up to 3 attempts, then amiodarone
t_svt_cv.text: Unstable regular narrow tachycardia: synchronised cardioversion now (100 J). Adenosine may be tried while the defibrillator is made ready, but never delay the shock.

t_vagal.text: Stable regular narrow tachycardia: first a vagal manoeuvre.

result: Shows flutter waves or P waves going on (atrial flutter / tachycardia)
src: RCUK25|Adenosine 6-12-18 mg, then verapamil or beta-blocker, then synchronised shock
ESC19-SVT|Acute therapy of narrow QRS tachycardia
t_aden.text: Then adenosine (if no asthma and no pre-excitation). Next options appear if it fails or is not available.

bullets.t: Pregnant: monitor the baby after any cardioversion; metoprolol is the preferred preventive drug (not atenolol).

t_svt_ok.text: Converted. Record a 12-lead ECG in sinus rhythm (look for a delta wave of WPW, and the QT). Check potassium and magnesium. Observe for 1-2 hours; refer to cardiology OPD (ablation if it recurs).
src: ESC19-SVT|After conversion: ECG in sinus rhythm; catheter ablation for recurrent SVT

t_fail.text: Not converted: get expert help now and refer (senior, cardiologist, NICVD).

src: ESC24-AF|Haemodynamically unstable AF: immediate electrical cardioversion
t_af_cv.text: Unstable AF or flutter: synchronised cardioversion now (AF 200 J, flutter 200 J). Heparin as soon as possible, but do not delay the shock.

t_af_dur.text: When did this AF / flutter start?
ans: 24 hours ago or more, or not known
src: ESC24-AF|Early cardioversion only if AF lasted less than 24 hours (otherwise anticoagulation or TOE first)
ESC24-AF|Acute rate control: beta-blocker, diltiazem / verapamil (LVEF over 40%), digoxin; amiodarone in selected cases
RCUK25|Narrow irregular: rate control by EF
t_af_rate.text: Rate control. The app skips drugs that are unsafe for this patient. Lenient target: resting heart rate under 110.

bullets.t: Pregnant: rhythm control is preferred; use LMWH (DOACs are contraindicated in pregnancy); continue anticoagulation 4 weeks after cardioversion.

t_af_ac_new.text: AF under 24 hours: start heparin (UFH or LMWH) unless contraindicated. Early cardioversion (electrical or drug) may be considered by the senior once stable; decide long-term anticoagulation with the CHA2DS2-VA score.

bullets.t: Pregnant: LMWH; DOACs are contraindicated; involve the obstetrician.

t_af_ac_old.text: AF for 24 hours or more, or unknown: do NOT cardiovert electively (stroke risk) unless unstable. Rate control; start heparin (UFH or LMWH); at least 3 weeks of anticoagulation, or TOE, before an elective cardioversion. Refer to cardiology.
src: ESC24-AF|Cardioversion of AF lasting over 24 h: 3 weeks of anticoagulation or imaging first

t_af_end.text: AF / flutter managed: rate controlled and anticoagulation decided.

t_af_ctrl.text: AF with a controlled rate: no urgent rate treatment. Find the cause, decide anticoagulation (CHA2DS2-VA), refer to cardiology OPD.

src: ESC19-SVT|MAT: treat the underlying condition (class I); verapamil, diltiazem or a beta-1 selective blocker (IIa)
t_mat.text: MAT: treat the cause first (lung disease, low oxygen, low potassium / magnesium, sepsis). Cardioversion does not work. Rate control only if needed:

t_mat_end.text: MAT controlled; keep treating the cause.

t_sinus.text: Sinus tachycardia: treat the cause (fever, pain, low volume, low oxygen, anaemia, sepsis, PE, thyroid, anxiety). Never cardiovert it or give antiarrhythmics to slow it.
src: AHA25-ALS|Box 1: assess whether the rate fits the condition
RCUK25|Synchronised shock up to 3 attempts, then amiodarone 300 mg or procainamide
t_vt_cv.text: Synchronised cardioversion (monomorphic VT 100 J; raise the energy if it fails, up to 3 attempts). If the pulse is lost: CPR and Code mode.

t_vt_q.help: AHA 2025: adenosine may be tried only if the rhythm is regular and monomorphic, to help diagnosis. Never verapamil or diltiazem for a wide tachycardia.
t_vt_q.text: Stable VT. Can a skilled doctor sedate the patient and cardiovert now?
src: ESC22-VA|Tolerated monomorphic VT: electrical cardioversion first if sedation risk is low (class I); IV procainamide (IIa) or amiodarone (IIb)
AHA25-ALS|Section 15 Rec 3 (procainamide, amiodarone, sotalol may be considered)
RCUK25|Procainamide 10-15 mg/kg, or amiodarone 300 mg if not available

t_vt_ok.text: Converted: 12-lead ECG, potassium and magnesium, look for ischaemia (chest pain flow), echo. Refer to cardiology / NICVD (cause, ICD assessment).
src: ESC22-VA|After VT: evaluation for structural heart disease
AHA25-ALS|Top message 8 and Electrical Cardioversion algorithm (polymorphic VT: unsynchronised high-energy shock)
t_poly.text: Polymorphic VT is always unstable: DEFIBRILLATE (unsynchronised) now. If the pulse is lost: CPR and Code mode.

src: RCUK25|Torsades: magnesium 8 mmol over 10 min; isoprenaline or pacing; avoid amiodarone
ESC22-VA|Torsades: magnesium, potassium, stop offending drugs
t_tdp.text: Torsades (long QT): magnesium. Correct potassium to 4.5-5.0. Stop QT-lengthening drugs. Do NOT give amiodarone.

src: RCUK25|Torsades: isoprenaline or temporary pacing to increase heart rate
ESC22-VA|Overdrive pacing / isoproterenol in acquired long QT
t_tdp_more.text: If it keeps coming back with slow heart rate or pauses: raise the heart rate.

t_tdp_end.text: Torsades treated: monitor, keep potassium 4.5-5.0 and magnesium normal, no QT-lengthening drugs; refer to cardiology.

src: ESC22-VA|Polymorphic VT in acute ischaemia: beta-blockers, amiodarone, urgent revascularisation
t_pmvt.text: Polymorphic VT with a normal QT: usually acute ischaemia. ECG for STEMI; urgent angiography (NICVD). To prevent recurrences:

t_pmvt_end.text: Refer to NICVD for urgent angiography. Open the chest pain flow if there is chest pain.

src: ESC19-SVT|Pre-excited AF: urgent electrical cardioversion if unstable
t_px_cv.text: Unstable pre-excited AF: synchronised cardioversion now (200 J).

t_px_drug.warn: No AV-node blockers in pre-excited AF.
src: ESC19-SVT|Pre-excited AF: ibutilide or procainamide (IIa), flecainide (IIb), cardioversion
RCUK25|AF with pre-excitation: procainamide or cardioversion
t_px_drug.text: Stable pre-excited AF. NEVER give adenosine, verapamil, diltiazem, beta-blockers, digoxin or IV amiodarone (they can cause VF).

t_px_ok.text: Converted: refer to NICVD / electrophysiology for ablation of the accessory pathway.

brady.title: Bradycardia with a pulse
brady.sub: Atropine, infusions and pacing, with alternatives

b_stab.text: Is the slow rhythm causing danger signs? Shock or low BP, fainting, ischaemic chest pain, heart failure, confused.

b_unstable.text: Unstable bradycardia: oxygen if SpO2 is low, IV access, 12-lead ECG, pacing pads on now. Look for causes: inferior MI, drugs (beta-blocker, calcium blocker, digoxin), high potassium, low oxygen.
src: AHA25-ALS|Bradycardia algorithm box 3 and possible causes
AHA25-ALS|Bradycardia algorithm box 5: atropine; if ineffective, transcutaneous pacing and/or dopamine or epinephrine infusion
RCUK25|Interim measures: atropine, isoprenaline, adrenaline, alternatives, transcutaneous pacing
b_atropine.text: Atropine first. If it does not work: transcutaneous pacing and/or an adrenaline or dopamine infusion. Pacing can be started at any time.

b_better.text: Better. Keep the pads on. High-grade block (Mobitz II, complete heart block, wide escape) needs transvenous / permanent pacing: refer to NICVD. Treat the cause.
src: AHA25-ALS|Bradycardia algorithm box 6: consider transvenous pacing, expert consultation

b_fail.text: Not responding: expert help and urgent transfer for transvenous pacing (NICVD).

b_risk.text: Is there a risk of asystole? Recent asystole, Mobitz II, complete heart block with wide QRS, or pauses over 3 seconds.

b_highrisk.text: High risk even if stable now: keep monitored with pacing pads on and atropine drawn up; refer for transvenous / permanent pacing (NICVD).
src: RCUK25|Risk of asystole: seek expert help, transvenous pacing

b_stable.text: Stable and low risk: observe on the monitor, 12-lead ECG, look for causes (drugs, potassium, thyroid, ischaemia; athletes and sleep).
src: AHA25-ALS|Bradycardia algorithm box 7: identify and treat causes, observe

b_avb1.text: First-degree AV block: no treatment. Review drugs (beta-blocker, calcium blocker, digoxin), potassium and ischaemia.

b_mob1_end.text: Mobitz I (Wenckebach): usually benign (often inferior MI or drugs). Observe; if symptoms appear treat as bradycardia.

arrest.title: Cardiac arrest (Code mode)
arrest.sub: ACLS with the team leader's clock and recorder

r_check.text: After ROSC: go through the checklist.

r_ecg.text: 12-lead ECG after ROSC: what does it show?
ans: No STEMI, but the patient is in shock

r_stemi.text: STEMI after ROSC: emergency angiography / PCI even if the patient is comatose. Refer to NICVD now.

src: AHA25-PCAC|Section 5 (MAP 65 or more) and Section 10 Rec 3
r_shock.text: Shock after ROSC: keep MAP 65 mmHg or more; consider urgent angiography (cardiogenic shock).

r_end_ref.text: Transfer to NICVD / ICU with a doctor.
src: AHA25-PCAC|Section 10 (angiography) and transfer to critical care

r_end.text: Continue post-arrest care in ICU / CCU; find the cause.

acs.title: Chest pain, ACS and STEMI
acs.sub: ECG in 10 minutes, red flags, thrombolysis or NICVD

c_ecg0.label: ECG done
c_ecg0.text: Record a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of arrival and show it to the doctor at once. Monitor, IV access, SpO2.
src: ESC23-ACS|ECG within 10 minutes of first medical contact

c_unst.text: Is the patient unstable? Shock or low BP, acute heart failure, dangerous arrhythmia.

c_red.text: Before treating as ACS, tick any red flag of another killer:
src: ESC23-ACS|Differential diagnosis of acute chest pain

c_aorta.warn: No thrombolysis, no heparin, no aspirin.
c_aorta.text: Suspected aortic dissection: NO fibrinolysis, NO heparin and NO antiplatelet drugs until it is excluded. Pain relief; heart rate under 60 and SBP under 120; urgent CT aorta; refer to NICVD (cardiac surgery).
src: AHAACC25-HBP|Section 6.2: SBP below 120 in the first hour in aortic dissection
ESC19-HTNEM|Acute aortic disease: SBP below 120 and HR below 60

c_tamp.text: Suspected tamponade: bedside echo now. Fluid bolus if low BP; avoid diuretics and nitrates; urgent pericardiocentesis (refer to NICVD if it cannot be done here).

c_pe.text: Possible pulmonary embolism: oxygen, anticoagulation per the PE protocol unless contraindicated, echo for a strained right ventricle, CT pulmonary angiography; refer. Shock with suspected PE is high-risk PE: thrombolysis is a senior decision.

c_ecg.help: STEMI: new ST elevation at the J point in 2 neighbouring leads, 1 mm or more (V2-V3: 2 mm men 40 or over, 2.5 mm men under 40, 1.5 mm women). Equivalents: posterior MI, new LBBB / paced rhythm with ongoing ischaemia. ST elevation in aVR with widespread ST depression: urgent angiography.
ans: ST elevation in 2 neighbouring leads (STEMI) or a STEMI equivalent
ST depression, T inversion, or changes that come and go
12-48 hours ago, still pain, heart failure, shock or arrhythmia
12-48 hours ago, now pain-free and stable
src: ESC23-ACS|Reperfusion: within 12 h; over 12 h with ongoing ischaemia primary PCI; 12-48 h routine PCI (IIa)

s_asp.text: Aspirin now (once aortic dissection is not suspected).

s_supp.text: Also now: oxygen only if SpO2 under 90%; defibrillator pads ready; send the ECG to NICVD. Pain?
ans: Ongoing pain: give a nitrate / pain relief
src: ESC23-ACS|Oxygen if SpO2 below 90%; nitrates and opioids for pain
ESC23-ACS|Nitrates; titrated IV opioids for severe pain
s_gtn.text: Pain relief: nitrate first (not if SBP under 90, right ventricular infarction or recent sildenafil / tadalafil), then morphine if needed.

s_pci.help: Count the call, loading the ambulance, the drive in today's traffic and the cath lab team arriving.
s_pci.text: Call NICVD now. Can the patient reach NICVD and have primary PCI within 120 minutes of this STEMI diagnosis?
src: ESC23-ACS|Primary PCI if it can be done within 120 min of diagnosis; otherwise fibrinolysis within 10 min
ACCAHA25-ACS|Reperfusion strategy (PCI within 120 min of first medical contact)

s_preg.text: Pregnant: primary PCI is preferred; fibrinolysis only if PCI cannot be done in time (pregnancy is a relative contraindication). Senior and obstetrician decide.
src: ESC25-PREG|§12.2.1.2 (systemic thrombolysis if timely PCI is not available)

s_ppci.text: Primary PCI at NICVD. Has NICVD asked you to give a P2Y12 drug or heparin before transfer?
src: ESC23-ACS|Pretreatment with a P2Y12 inhibitor before primary PCI may be considered (IIb)

s_ufh.text: Heparin before transfer (only if NICVD asked):

s_xfer.text: Transfer to NICVD now: doctor, monitor, defibrillator, oxygen; the ECGs and this record (times of every drug).

s_cx_no.text: Fibrinolysis is contraindicated: transfer to NICVD for PCI even if it takes longer.

s_cx_rel.text: Relative contraindication: the senior weighs the benefit against the bleeding risk. If NICVD PCI is possible even with delay, transfer may be safer.

src: ESC23-ACS|Fibrinolysis within 12 h of symptoms when primary PCI cannot be done within 120 min; start within 10 min; fibrin-specific agent preferred
s_lysis.text: Fibrinolysis within 10 minutes of the STEMI diagnosis (pain within 12 hours). First available agent:

s_l_ap.text: With fibrinolysis: clopidogrel (with the aspirin already given).

src: ESC23-ACS|Anticoagulation with fibrinolysis until revascularisation (up to 8 days)
s_l_ac.text: With fibrinolysis: anticoagulant (UFH is the CEC's usual drug).

s_l_watch.text: 60-90 minutes after the fibrinolytic: has the ST elevation fallen by more than half, with the pain gone?
ans: No: failed, or shock / pain returns
src: ESC23-ACS|Assess ST resolution at 60-90 min; rescue PCI if it fails

s_l_ok.text: Successful: transfer to NICVD for angiography within 2-24 hours.

s_rescue.text: Failed fibrinolysis: immediate transfer to NICVD for rescue PCI.

s_late1.text: Over 12 hours with ongoing ischaemia, heart failure, shock or arrhythmia: primary PCI is still indicated. Refer to NICVD now. No fibrinolysis.
src: ESC23-ACS|Over 12 h with ongoing symptoms: primary PCI (class I)

s_late2.text: 12-48 hours, pain-free and stable: refer to NICVD for angiography / PCI (within 12-48 hours).

s_late.text: Over 48 hours and pain-free: no emergency reperfusion. Refer to NICVD / cardiology for assessment.

n_risk.text: Any very-high-risk feature? Shock or low BP; pain that keeps coming back or does not settle; life-threatening arrhythmia or arrest; acute heart failure; ST elevation that comes and goes.
src: ESC23-ACS|Very high-risk NSTE-ACS: immediate invasive strategy (within 2 h)

n_vhr.text: Very high risk: immediate angiography (within 2 hours). Aspirin, then transfer to NICVD now.

src: ESC23-ACS|Parenteral anticoagulation for all NSTE-ACS at diagnosis
n_ac.text: Anticoagulant (UFH is the CEC's usual drug):

n_poss.text: Could this still be ACS (typical pain, risk factors, age)?

n_asp_p.text: Aspirin (unless contraindicated) while you repeat the ECG:

n_serial.text: No troponin test at the CEC. Repeat the ECG every 15-30 minutes while there is pain, and at once if pain returns. What does the repeat ECG show?
ans: New or changing ST depression / T changes
No change, but ACS is still possible
src: ESC23-ACS|Repeat ECG in recurrent symptoms or diagnostic uncertainty
UDMI5|Troponin is needed to diagnose MI

n_ac2.text: Dynamic ECG changes: start the anticoagulant now.

n_early.text: Dynamic ECG changes = high risk: early invasive strategy (within 24 hours). Refer to NICVD today.
src: ESC23-ACS|High-risk NSTE-ACS: early invasive strategy within 24 h

n_trop.text: ACS cannot be ruled out here (no troponin): refer to NICVD (or a hospital with high-sensitivity troponin) today. Do not send home.
src: UDMI5|Definition of myocardial injury and MI (troponin)

n_other.text: Treat the other cause; if pain returns, repeat the ECG at once.

hf.title: Heart failure: pulmonary oedema and cardiogenic shock

ans: Breathless with crackles; BP normal or high (acute pulmonary oedema)
Low BP (SBP under 90) with cold, clammy skin, confusion or little urine (cardiogenic shock)
Swelling and breathlessness worsening over days; BP normal (congestion)
src: ESC26-HF|Section 7: clinical presentations of decompensated HF

bullets.t: Pregnant or recently delivered: think of peripartum cardiomyopathy and pre-eclampsia; no ACE inhibitor, ARB or ARNI in pregnancy; call the obstetrician.

h_apo.text: Now: sit upright, monitor, IV access, ECG (STEMI? arrhythmia?), bedside echo. Oxygen if SpO2 under 90%; CPAP / non-invasive ventilation if breathing fast (over 25) with SpO2 under 90%. Find the trigger: ACS, very high BP, arrhythmia, valve problem, infection, PE, missed medicines.
src: ESC26-HF|Section 7, Figure 13: initial management of decompensated HF
ESC19-HTNEM|Pulmonary oedema: SBP below 140 at once
ESC19-HTNEM|Acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema: nitroglycerine or nitroprusside with a loop diuretic
h_hi.text: Hypertensive pulmonary oedema: bring SBP below 140 at once with a nitrate, plus the loop diuretic.

src: ESC26-HF|Figure 13: consider vasodilators when SBP > 110 mmHg

h_diur_lo.text: SBP 90-110: loop diuretic only (no nitrate); watch the BP.

h_resp.text: After 1-2 hours: good urine (over 100-150 mL/hour) and breathing better?
src: ESC26-HF|Assess diuretic response (urine output; urinary sodium-guided therapy IIb)
ESC21-HF|Poor response: urine output below 100 mL/h in the first 6 hours

h_ok.text: Responding. Continue; when stable restart / start the heart failure medicines, including an SGLT2 inhibitor in hospital (ESC 2026 class I).
src: ESC26-HF|In-hospital SGLT2 inhibitor after stabilisation (class I)

h_poor.text: Poor response: double the IV loop diuretic; consider adding acetazolamide or a thiazide; check for low BP / poor perfusion (shock); refer to CCU (NICVD).

h_shock.text: Cardiogenic shock: ECG (STEMI: urgent PCI, refer to NICVD now); bedside echo (mechanical complication, tamponade, right ventricular infarct). Fluid 200-250 mL over 15-30 min only if no congestion. Then a vasopressor; transfer to NICVD (Shock Team).
src: ESC21-HF|Fluid challenge (200 mL or more over 15-30 min) if no overt fluid overload

h_press.text: Vasopressor for MAP 65 mmHg or more:

h_ino.text: Still low output (cold, little urine) with MAP 65 or more?
src: ESC26-HF|Inotropes for low output with hypoperfusion

h_shock_end.text: Transfer to NICVD (Shock Team) with a doctor.
src: ESC26-HF|Shock Team; temporary MCS in selected patients

bp.title: Very high blood pressure
bp.sub: Emergency vs urgency; dissection, pulmonary oedema, ACS, stroke, pregnancy

p_conf.text: Repeat the BP after 5 minutes of rest (correct cuff, both arms). Still 180/110 or more (160/110 or more if pregnant or recently delivered)?
src: AHAACC25-HBP|Section 6.2 (above 180 and/or 120 with organ damage = emergency)

p_low.text: Not severe now: usual care and follow-up.

p_preg.text: Severe hypertension in pregnancy or after delivery: treat within 30-60 minutes and lower gradually to below 160/110 (not too fast). Continuous foetal monitoring. Call the obstetrician. Signs of pre-eclampsia (headache, visual change, upper abdominal pain, fits): magnesium sulfate.
src: ESC25-PREG|§12.3.3 (admit; reduce gradually below 160/110; continuous CTG)
ESC25-PREG|§12.3.3: oral nifedipine, labetalol or methyldopa; IV labetalol (or nicardipine); hydralazine second-line

p_preg_mg.text: Pre-eclampsia with severe features, or a fit?

p_preg_end.text: Refer as an obstetric emergency with the drugs given written down.

p_tod.text: Tick any sign of acute organ damage:
src: AHAACC25-HBP|Section 6.2: hypertensive emergency = severe BP with acute target-organ damage

p_urg.text: No acute organ damage: do NOT lower the BP quickly. Rest 30 minutes and recheck; restart or adjust oral medicines; review within days. Never sublingual nifedipine capsules.
src: AHAACC25-HBP|Severe hypertension without target-organ damage: no rapid lowering; oral therapy

p_emerg.text: Hypertensive emergency (encephalopathy, malignant hypertension, kidney injury): ICU care. Lower SBP by no more than 25% in the first hour, then to 160/100 over the next 2-6 hours, then to normal over 24-48 hours.

src: ESC19-HTNEM|Labetalol or nicardipine first; nitroprusside or urapidil as alternatives

p_icu.text: Transfer to an ICU with titratable IV drugs and monitoring.

p_aorta.warn: No thrombolysis, no heparin, no aspirin.
p_aorta.text: Aortic dissection: heart rate under 60 and SBP under 120 within the first hour. Beta-blocker FIRST (before any vasodilator), pain relief, urgent CT, refer to NICVD (cardiac surgery). No fibrinolysis, anticoagulant or antiplatelet drug.
src: AHAACC25-HBP|Section 6.2: SBP below 120 in the first hour (aortic dissection)
ESC19-HTNEM|Acute aortic disease: SBP below 120, HR below 60; esmolol plus a vasodilator, or labetalol

p_ao_vq.text: Heart rate now under 60 but SBP still 120 or more?

p_ao_end.text: Refer to NICVD now (cardiac surgery) with BP control continued.

src: ESC19-HTNEM|Acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema: SBP below 140 immediately
p_apo.text: Pulmonary oedema with high BP: SBP below 140 at once with a nitrate, plus a loop diuretic.

p_apo_end.text: Continue in the heart failure flow / CCU.

src: ESC19-HTNEM|Acute coronary event: SBP below 140 immediately; nitroglycerine, labetalol
p_acs.text: ACS with high BP: SBP below 140 at once: nitrate or labetalol. Then follow the chest pain flow.

p_acs_go.text: Open the chest pain flow now?

src: ESC19-HTNEM|Stroke targets (ischaemic with / without thrombolysis; haemorrhagic)
p_stroke.text: Stroke: refer to a stroke centre now (CT). Ischaemic and clot-busting planned: BP below 185/110 before and below 180/105 after; not planned: lower only if above 220/120, by about 15% in the first hour. Brain bleed with SBP over 180: lower to 130-180.

src: ESC19-HTNEM|Sympathomimetic crisis and pheochromocytoma: phentolamine; benzodiazepines; avoid beta-blockers alone
p_sym.text: Cocaine / amphetamine or pheochromocytoma: calm and sedate first (benzodiazepine); avoid a beta-blocker on its own (it can raise BP further). Phentolamine if available; otherwise a nitrate or nicardipine.

code.energy: Biphasic: the dose your defibrillator's maker advises (often 120-200 J); if unknown, the maximum. Monophasic: 360 J. Same or higher for later shocks.
cpr: Push hard: at least 5 cm; push fast: 100-120 per minute; full recoil; minimal pauses.
No advanced airway: 30 compressions to 2 breaths.
Advanced airway: 1 breath every 6 seconds (10/min) with continuous compressions; waveform capnography.
Change the compressor every 2 minutes, or sooner if tired.
Access: IV first; IO if IV fails or is not possible (AHA 2025).
preg: Manual left uterine displacement throughout CPR (when the top of the womb is at or above the umbilicus).
Prepare for resuscitative delivery from the start: if no ROSC, deliver the baby aiming to finish by 5 minutes after the arrest.
On IV magnesium sulfate: give calcium (10 mL calcium chloride 10% or 30 mL calcium gluconate 10%).
src: AHA25-ALS|Adult Cardiac Arrest Algorithm 2025 (CPR quality, shock energy, drug therapy, every 2 minutes)
AHA25-SPEC|§19.3 cardiac arrest in pregnancy (left uterine displacement, delivery by 5 minutes, arm IV access, calcium with magnesium, no foetal monitoring)
code.epiNote: AHA 2025: in VF / pVT give epinephrine after the first shocks fail (the algorithm shows it after the 2nd shock); in asystole / PEA as soon as possible; then every 3-5 minutes. ERC / RCUK 2025: after the 3rd shock in VF / pVT.
code.antiNote: Amiodarone 300 mg (or lidocaine 1-1.5 mg/kg) after the 3rd shock; amiodarone 150 mg (or lidocaine 0.5-0.75 mg/kg) after the 5th.

scenarios.title: VF arrest in the CEC
scenarios.story: A 58-year-old man with chest pain collapses on the bed. No pulse. The monitor shows VF.
teach: Shock at once for VF; CPR immediately after each shock.
Epinephrine after the 2nd shock (AHA), every 3-5 min.
Rhythm checks every 2 minutes, pauses under 10 seconds.

scenarios.title: PEA from hyperkalaemia (dialysis patient)
scenarios.story: A 45-year-old woman on dialysis missed two sessions, felt weak and collapsed. No pulse. Monitor: slow wide complexes.

rules.rhythm: Sinus rhythm 80/min with peaked T waves, BP 100/60: ROSC

teach: Non-shockable: epinephrine as soon as possible.
Think of Hs and Ts: hyperkalaemia in a dialysis patient.
Calcium, insulin with glucose, bicarbonate; then dialysis.

scenarios.title: Stable SVT
scenarios.story: A 28-year-old woman with sudden palpitations for 40 minutes. BP 118/76, alert, no chest pain.

rules.msg: After 12 mg the monitor shows a few seconds of pause, then sinus rhythm.

teach: Stable: vagal manoeuvre first, then adenosine 6 mg, then 12 mg.

scenarios.title: Unstable bradycardia: complete heart block
scenarios.story: A 68-year-old man feels faint. HR 32, BP 74/40, cold and clammy. ECG: complete heart block with wide escape.

rules.msg: Little change after atropine (common in wide-escape complete block).

teach: Atropine first, but do not delay pacing in wide-escape complete heart block.

scenarios.title: Torsades de pointes
scenarios.story: A 45-year-old woman on azithromycin and ondansetron has fainting spells. Runs of twisting wide QRS; QTc 560 ms between runs.

monitor.rhythm: Runs of polymorphic VT; QTc 560 ms

set.rhythm: Sinus rhythm 76/min, QTc 540 ms, no runs

rules.msg: Amiodarone lengthened the QT: the runs come more often.

teach: Magnesium 2 g; potassium 4.5-5.0; stop QT drugs; never amiodarone.

scenarios.title: Pre-excited AF
scenarios.story: A 24-year-old man with palpitations. Irregular wide tachycardia 240/min with changing QRS shapes. BP 104/66, alert.

rules.msg: An AV-node blocker in pre-excited AF: the rhythm turned into VF!

set.rhythm: Sinus rhythm 90/min with a delta wave

teach: Never AV-node blockers or IV amiodarone in pre-excited AF.

scenarios.title: STEMI with a contraindication to thrombolysis
scenarios.story: A 60-year-old man, anterior STEMI, pain for 2 hours. NICVD can take him but the drive is about 3 hours today. He had an ischaemic stroke 2 months ago.
want: ans:c_ecg=ST elevation in 2 neighbouring leads (STEMI) or a STEMI equivalent
teach: Ischaemic stroke within 6 months is an absolute contraindication (ESC).
Transfer for PCI even if delayed.

scenarios.title: Acute pulmonary oedema with very high BP
scenarios.story: A 70-year-old woman, sudden breathlessness at night, frothy sputum. BP 196/112, SpO2 84%, crackles to mid-zones.
teach: Sit up, oxygen / CPAP, nitrate to SBP below 140, loop diuretic.

scenarios.title: Very high BP with aortic dissection red flags
scenarios.story: A 52-year-old man with sudden tearing pain to the back. BP right arm 210/120, left arm 168/96.
teach: Beta-blocker first, then vasodilator; HR under 60, SBP under 120; no antiplatelet or anticoagulant.

src: ERC25-ALS|ALS: minimise pauses (under 10 s); defibrillate rapidly
rules: First shock within 3 minutes of a shockable rhythm (RCUK / ERC 2025).
Pauses for rhythm or pulse checks under 10 seconds.
Epinephrine: as soon as possible in asystole / PEA; after the 2nd shock in VF / pVT (AHA; ERC: 3rd); every 3-5 minutes.
Antiarrhythmic after the 3rd shock in VF / pVT.
